title: U2AF1 mutations rescue deleterious exon skipping induced by KRAS mutations.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and opened all three processed files of GEO series GSE328821 (short-read RNA-seq, 53 samples): each is a gene-level read-count table with 58,735 genes (Ensembl IDs) by 5, 28 and 21 sample columns, plus gene annotation columns. Also opened the long-read transcript count table of GSE328804 (12 samples, 436,441 transcript rows, IsoQuant/StringTie counts). Listed the remaining file (25 MB merged GTF annotation). No exon-level or splicing (percent-spliced-in) tables are deposited.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Abstract only: the paper is paywalled, has no PMCID, and no supplement was retrievable. The pan-cancer splicing-factor/oncogene co-occurrence analysis and the KRAS exon-skipping measurements are described in the abstract but their tables were not seen.

a1_downloadable.note: GEO processed files download openly (checked); raw reads in SRA. Supplementary tables of the paywalled article were not retrievable.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Checked files: only gene-level counts and long-read transcript counts. Any splicing label (exon skipping per exon, U2AF1-sensitive 3' splice sites) would have to be constructed by re-aligning raw reads and running a splicing caller; the only ready labels are sample genotypes.

a3_inputs_present.note: Ensembl gene and transcript IDs present; sequences would need genome lookup but that is routine.

a4_units_stated.note: Raw integer read counts (short-read) and grouped counts (long-read); units implicit but standard.

a5_enough_rows.note: Unit of observation is the sample: 53 short-read plus 12 long-read samples (counted in files) across a handful of genotypes in two cell lines (A549, H441). Far below the 400-row classification floor.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Processed files are small; the raw reads needed to build splicing labels are excluded by policy.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: GEO metadata says 53 and 12 samples; the file headers sum to 54 short-read columns (one cell line duplicated across files) and 12 long-read columns, consistent.

a8_label_provenance.note: Genotypes come from prime editing, a physical intervention; not model-derived.

existing_models.name: SpliceAI (general splicing predictor from DNA sequence, Jaganathan et al., Cell 2019)
existing_models.score_and_split: Predicts splice sites genome-wide, evaluated on held-out chromosomes; not specific to splicing-factor-mutant cells.

existing_models.name: Pangolin (tissue-aware splicing predictor, Genome Biology 2022)
existing_models.score_and_split: Splice-site usage across tissues; not trained on U2AF1-mutant contexts.

backbone.name: SpliceAI or Pangolin (sequence-to-splicing models) would be the natural backbone

integration.partner_dataset: TCGA / AACR GENIE mutation calls (for co-occurrence), not deposited with this paper
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Which oncogene mutations create splicing defects that splicing-factor mutations are selected to rescue — but the labels needed to model it are not in the deposited files.

controls.positive_control: KRAS exon 2 skipping in KRAS G12S cells reverted by U2AF1 S34F (from abstract only).
controls.negative_control: Parental and back-edited wild-type U2AF1 clones (seen as sample columns).

honest_claim_h3: With ~65 samples of gene-level counts, a model could at best classify the U2AF1 genotype of an A549 or H441 clone from its expression profile, which is neither hard nor useful.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the DNA sequence around each exon to predict whether a cancer splicing-factor mutation changes that exon's inclusion.
plain_idea.train_on: Sequence windows around 3' splice sites, labelled by splicing change between mutant and wild-type cells; the number of labelled exons is unknown because no exon-level table is deposited.
plain_idea.predict: Whether each exon is skipped more or less in U2AF1-mutant cells; the true answer would have to be computed from raw RNA-seq reads, which are not processed in the deposit.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Cancer biologists could flag which oncogene mutations create splicing defects that splicing-factor mutations rescue, but the labels would have to be built from raw reads first.

ml_idea: Predict U2AF1-mutant-sensitive splicing events from splice-site sequence, with a frozen SpliceAI-style backbone plus a head. Not feasible from the deposited files: they hold only gene-level and transcript-level counts for 65 samples, so exon-level labels would need re-alignment of raw reads.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; rejected at Part A. Processed tables are ~11 MB compressed (checked).
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Look for an exon-level splicing table in GEO: none exists (checked), so labels need raw-read processing.

verdict_reason: Fails A2 and A5 (checked in the files). The GEO deposit holds only gene-level counts for 53 short-read samples and transcript counts for 12 long-read samples. Any splicing label would have to be built from raw sequencing reads, and the sample-level unit gives about 65 rows.
